context: OpenSecureAIAlliance/RFCs#6 — pre-connection tool-trust attestation as SAFE evidence. These vectors exercise the reviewer's correction: a signed coverage block binds the signer to the coverage assertion, not to the fact that the checks ran. Signature validity, coverage/aggregation consistency, and execution-evidence status are three separate properties, and none inherits another's result.
status: proposed for discussion (schema not yet fixed upstream). Signature validity is assumed valid in every vector, because the property under test is coverage and execution, not the signature.

report_shape.target_ref: stable identity of the graded artifact (MCP URL / package coordinate / repo + content digest)
report_shape.definition_digest: sha-256 of the tool definition this report was produced against
report_shape.verdict: { grade, score, verdict_digest, attestation } — the signed, offline-recomputable verdict (RFC 8785 JCS + RFC 7515 JWS)

coverage.checks: [ { id, required: bool, state: pass|fail|skipped|not-run, execution_evidence: reproduced|referenced|none } ]

consumer_dimensions.signature: valid | invalid — under the consumer's trust policy
consumer_dimensions.coverage_consistency: consistent | inconsistent — declared checks vs the aggregation, and whether a required check was skipped or not-run
consumer_dimensions.execution: verified | reproduced | unavailable | insufficient — was execution evidence for the required checks independently checkable
consumer_dimensions.admission: proceed | hold — a SEPARATELY VERSIONED policy, not a change to the evidence verdict

vectors.name: skipped-required-check
vectors.property: A valid signature over a report that explicitly records a required check as skipped.
vectors.why: The signature binds the assertion that one required check was skipped; it does not make the skip go away. A coverage reader sees required_passed < required_total with a skipped required check and reports inconsistent. Admission holds under any policy that requires all required checks to run.

vectors.name: completion-without-execution-evidence
vectors.property: A valid signature claiming completion, with correct arithmetic, but no independently checkable execution evidence for the required checks. THE DISTINGUISHING CONTROL.
vectors.why: Signature and arithmetic both pass — a coverage-only reader passes this. The false green: every required check reads pass, but none carries execution evidence, so nothing establishes the checks actually ran. Only the execution dimension catches it. Whether a consumer may proceed on a signed-but-unevidenced report is a separately versioned admission policy, not a change to the evidence verdict.

vectors.name: definition-digest-mismatch
vectors.property: A report produced for definition digest A, presented when admission observes digest B.
vectors.why: Everything about the report is sound — for the wrong subject. The report's definition_digest (A) does not match what admission observes (B), so a valid, fully-evidenced report about definition A says nothing about the definition being connected. Binding the subject inside the signed report is what lets the consumer catch this.

vectors.name: reproduction-unavailable
vectors.property: A required check whose execution evidence is referenced, but the inputs or dependencies cannot be disclosed, so the reference does not resolve.
vectors.why: Distinct from completion-without-execution-evidence: here evidence IS referenced, but the reference does not resolve because inputs or dependencies cannot be disclosed. The consumer cannot reproduce, so execution is unavailable rather than insufficient — a different outcome the reader must keep separate, exactly as an unresolvable reference is distinct from a missing one.

vectors.name: positive-continuation
vectors.property: Matching definition, all required checks pass with reproduced execution evidence, declared policy satisfied.
vectors.why: All three dimensions pass on their own — signature valid, coverage consistent, execution reproduced — against the definition being connected. This is the only vector where admission proceeds, and it proceeds because every dimension was checked independently, not because any one inherited another's result.
